summary.title: 12-Week Bench Press Strength Builder — Upper/Lower
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You came in with a 275lb bench press target — I've built the entire program around getting you there. Week 1 is your calibration week — the weights are set conservatively so you can focus on form and give me honest effort ratings after each set. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy — 5×5 bench at 170lbs, log effort honestly.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary strength movement — 5×5 at 75% of your 1RM establishes your Week 1 baseline and gives me honest performance data to build the next 11 weeks on.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Develops mid-back thickness and lat strength — a strong upper back is the foundation your bench presses off of, keeping your scapulae retracted and stable under load.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest and anterior delt development through the incline pressing pattern — builds the supplementary chest mass that contributes to your bench press strength ceiling.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pulling movement for lat width and strength — the lats play a direct role in stabilising the bar path during your bench press descent.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Lateral head tricep isolation for lockout strength — the triceps are the primary mover in the top third of your bench press, and direct work here builds the strength you need to lock out heavier loads.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work to balance the horizontal pressing volume — mandatory shoulder health maintenance for any athlete pushing a bench press 1RM up over 12 weeks.

sessions.title: Lower Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline lower — calibrate your squat and hinge with 5 sets.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral knee-dominant strength movement — builds total body strength and neural drive that supports your pressing performance through systemic hormonal adaptation.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — targets the biceps femoris and semimembranosus in a way that hip hinge patterns cannot fully replicate.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation through terminal knee extension — finishes quad training with focused muscle tension that compound movements leave partially unstimulated.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — builds the bracing strength needed to maintain a rigid torso under heavy squat and deadlift loads.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 5×8 bench at 145lbs, chase technique.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Second weekly exposure to your target lift at 85% of heavy-day load — higher reps build hypertrophy and technique reinforcement that directly feeds strength gains on your Monday heavy sets.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pulling for mid-back thickness and scapular retractor strength — keeps the upper back strong and balanced against the increased pressing volume this week.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range of motion — direct carryover to bench lockout, where a stronger close-grip translates to heavier loads locked out on your main lift.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pulling with a supinated grip that shifts emphasis toward the lower lats and biceps — complements the overhand row earlier in the week for full lat development.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Bicep curl for elbow flexor mass and strength — the biceps act as a secondary mover in all pulling exercises and direct work here builds the arm volume that supports your back training.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation for shoulder health and rotator cuff balance — a second weekly dose of posterior shoulder work to protect the joint through the increased pressing load of this program.

sessions.title: Lower Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — hamstring and glute focus, log effort on each set.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute-dominant movement through hip extension — builds posterior chain power that supports squat and deadlift performance while directly training the glutes in their strongest range.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that trains the hamstrings under a long eccentric stretch — develops the posterior chain strength and length that supports heavier squats on your Monday heavy lower session.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation at a stretched hip position — the seated curl applies tension at a longer muscle length than lying variations, targeting biceps femoris growth more completely.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Glute medius isolation for hip stability — strengthens the lateral hip stabilisers that keep your knees tracking correctly under load during squats.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core strengthening through a long lever rollout — develops the deep abdominal bracing strength needed to stay rigid under heavy squat and pressing loads.

sessions.title: Heavy Squat

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary strength movement for this entire plan. 300lbs is 82% of your current 1RM — heavy enough to build strength, conservative enough to establish a reliable baseline for Week 2 loading decisions.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Glute-dominant hip extension movement — directly strengthens the glutes at the top of the squat where drive and lockout occur, a key weak-point area for advanced squatters chasing a 40lb PR.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — complements the RDL hip-hinge pattern and ensures full hamstring development across both joint actions.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation through knee extension — directly targets the rectus femoris and VMO, muscles critical for knee stability and quad lockout strength in the squat.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — a braced, rigid core is essential for maintaining spinal position under a heavy squat bar, particularly at the sticking point.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Calf plantar flexion strength and ankle stability — ankle rigidity and calf strength support proper squat mechanics and balance at the bottom position.

sessions.title: Upper Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline upper heavy — calibrate bench and row loading today.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal push for upper body strength development — upper body pressing power and thoracic rigidity both contribute to a stable bar path and braced upper back position in the squat.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Heavy horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness and lat strength — upper back strength is directly tied to bar stability and preventing forward lean under a heavy squat.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width and strength — lats create upper back rigidity and control bar placement on the back squat, making this a meaningful accessory for a squatter.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest hypertrophy through the incline pressing pattern — builds balanced chest development and adds upper pressing volume without duplicating the flat bench stimulus.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical push for anterior and medial delt strength — shoulder pressing strength supports the bar shelf position and overall upper body structural integrity needed for heavy squats.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the horizontal pressing volume and maintains shoulder joint health through a high-volume pressing and squatting program.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout and builds overall pressing mass for the upper heavy days.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core challenge that builds the anterior core strength and spinal stiffness required to maintain a vertical torso position under a heavy squat bar.

sessions.title: Volume Squat
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — 5×8 squat at 255lbs, own every rep.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Second weekly squat exposure at 85% of Monday's heavy load — higher rep sets at this weight build work capacity and technical consistency under fatigue, both essential for a long-term squat strength peak.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg quad and glute strength that corrects bilateral asymmetries — addressing side-to-side imbalances is critical for advanced squatters looking to add significant load to the bar.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation in the seated position that emphasises the long head through a greater stretch — adds hamstring isolation volume to complement the RDL's hip-hinge stimulus.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher targeting the VMO and rectus femoris — builds quad hypertrophy that supports knee stability and power through the bottom of the squat.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core stability that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers to resist twisting under load — rotational stiffness is a key contributor to safe, powerful squatting.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains hip flexor strength and lower abdominal control — builds the anterior core capacity to maintain pelvic position during high-rep squat sets.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the soleus through the bent-knee position — pairs with standing calf work earlier in the week to develop both heads of the calf for complete lower leg strength and ankle stability.

sessions.title: Upper Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — 4×10 bench and back, build the base.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest hypertrophy through the incline pressing angle — a second weekly pressing stimulus at higher reps builds chest mass and volume capacity that supports heavier bench loads on heavy day.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that develops mid-back thickness and scapular retraction strength — upper back volume here directly supports the stable bar shelf position required for heavy squatting.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull with a reverse grip that emphasises the lower lats and bicep integration — broadens back development and adds vertical pull volume without duplicating the wide-grip stimulus from Tuesday.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral chest pressing that allows greater range of motion and addresses side-to-side pressing imbalances — adds hypertrophy volume to the chest without the barbell fatigue of a second heavy pressing day.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Bicep strength and mass through elbow flexion — direct arm volume on the upper volume day builds the elbow flexor size and strength that supports heavy rowing and pulling movements.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep long head hypertrophy through elbow extension at a stretch — targets the largest head of the tricep for mass development that supports all pressing movements in this program.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Medial delt isolation for shoulder width — compound pressing alone will not develop this head, and shoulder width and stability are both relevant for a secure, comfortable bar position on the back squat.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral-grip curl that targets the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the bicep — builds arm thickness and forearm strength that improves grip and elbow stability under heavy loads.

sessions.title: Lower Hypertrophy
sessions.sessionFocus: Lower hypertrophy — posterior chain focus, 3×12 RDL and hip thrust.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute hypertrophy movement through hip extension at a loaded stretch — glute strength at the top of the squat is a significant driver of the final push to lockout, and this is the best isolation tool for that position.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that builds hamstring and glute strength through their full range of motion — third weekly posterior chain exposure that targets hamstring hypertrophy to support squat depth and control on the way down.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — complements the hip-hinge RDL to ensure both joint actions of the hamstring are trained, building complete hamstring mass and reducing injury risk.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Glute medius and hip abductor isolation — lateral hip strength prevents knee cave and valgus collapse at the bottom of the squat, a common technical breakdown point as load increases.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Glute and hamstring accessory through a cable-resisted hip hinge — reinforces the hip hinge pattern with constant tension and trains glute activation through the full hip extension range.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Gastrocnemius development through full plantar flexion — calf strength contributes to ankle rigidity and balance in the squat, and dedicated hypertrophy work builds lower leg mass that supports the whole kinetic chain.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Soleus isolation through the bent-knee position — the soleus is the deeper calf muscle and responds best to seated loading, giving complete calf development when paired with standing calf raises.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability with a contralateral limb challenge — trains the deep stabilisers to maintain a neutral lumbar spine position, directly relevant to protecting the lower back under a loaded barbell.

exercises.coachingNote: Chest isolation with constant tension through the full range of motion — keeps mechanical tension on the pec when pressing fatigue makes heavy compound work harder to execute cleanly.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press

exercises.name: Face Pull

sessions.title: Legs Full
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration leg day — 4 sets squat, log your honest RPE.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral squat pattern — develops quad, glute, and core strength under load and serves as the main lower body compound stimulus for this session.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Glute-dominant movement at full hip extension — trains the glutes in a range that squats and RDLs underload, adding direct glute hypertrophy volume to this session.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semitendinosus in a way the RDL hip hinge cannot fully replicate, rounding out posterior chain development.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher that trains the rectus femoris through its full knee-extension range — compound squat patterns alone leave this portion of quad development incomplete.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise

sessions.title: Shoulders & Arms
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume arms day — 4 sets each on biceps and triceps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing done on Day 1 does not adequately stimulate the lateral head, so dedicated isolation work here fills that gap.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bicep compound that develops the short head and overall bicep thickness under a fixed bilateral grip — the most load you can move through a curl pattern, making it the anchor of this arms session.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment spreads at the bottom of the movement to maximise lateral head contraction — trains the tricep in a high-contraction, low-fatigue pattern that accumulates volume without residual shoulder stress.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Incline position puts the long head of the bicep on stretch at the start of every rep — this lengthened position is one of the strongest drivers of hypertrophy and complements the short-head barbell curl bias.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a fully lengthened state — research consistently shows stretched-position training produces superior hypertrophy, making this the most important tricep exercise for long head mass.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip shifts emphasis to the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the long head — adds arm thickness and forearm development that supinated curl variations leave undertrained.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation through horizontal abduction — the machine path locks in consistent form and keeps tension on the posterior deltoid throughout, balancing the pressing volume distributed across the week.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior chain volume — hamstrings and glutes, 4 sets each.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that maximises hamstring stretch at the bottom by keeping the legs straighter than a Romanian deadlift — provides a distinct stimulus from the RDL used mid-week and anchors the posterior chain session.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine path keeps glute tension consistent through the full hip extension range — gives the glutes a second dedicated session this week at a higher rep range than the barbell hip thrust, driving hypertrophy through volume.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hamstring in a lengthened state throughout the set compared to the lying variation used on Day 2 — alternating between these two curl positions across the week ensures full hamstring fiber recruitment.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Cable-loaded hip hinge that keeps constant tension on the glutes and hamstrings through the drive phase — the forward lean and cable angle bias the glute at the peak of extension in a way barbell hip thrusts do not.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Straight-leg position targets the gastrocnemius — the larger of the two calf muscles and the one responsible for visible calf mass. Direct plantar flexion work is the only way to develop this muscle.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Bent-knee position takes the gastrocnemius out of the movement and isolates the soleus — pairing this with the standing variation in the same session ensures both heads of the calf are fully trained.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core movement that trains the entire anterior chain under a long moment arm — significantly more demanding than a plank and builds the deep spinal stability needed to brace correctly under heavy compound loads.

summary.title: PPL 6-Day Advanced Hypertrophy — Quad, Hamstring & Glute Priority
summary.jordanWelcome: I'm Jordan, your coach for the next 12 weeks. You want to bring up your quads, hamstrings, glutes — I've structured your week so those muscles get trained fresh and with full focus, not as an afterthought, and in Week 1 you set your own starting weights in the app, so aim for something that feels like RPE 7-8 on each exercise. Week 1 is your calibration week — pick loads that match your effort targets and record them after each set; that data is how I tune what comes next. I'll use your RPE data from this week to tune what comes next specifically to you — the more honest you are, the better your plan gets.

sessions.title: Push Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy push — 5 sets on bench, calibrate effort.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal push compound for the session — trains the pecs, front delts, and triceps through a full pressing range, forming the foundation of your heavy push day.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts the stimulus onto the upper, clavicular head of the pec — a region that compounds flat pressing underserves and that contributes significantly to chest fullness.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid head for shoulder width — horizontal pressing alone does not sufficiently load this portion of the delt, making direct lateral work mandatory for full shoulder development.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (High to Low)
exercises.coachingNote: Hits the lower chest fibers through continuous cable tension across the full range of motion — a stimulus the barbell bench press cannot replicate due to diminishing tension at the top of the lift.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Tricep strength through the full press range — direct carryover to bench lockout and a strong mass-building stimulus for the lateral and medial tricep heads under load.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the long head of the triceps with the arm overhead-adjacent position — the long head is the largest of the three tricep heads and is often undertrained by pushdown-only approaches.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Cable tension keeps constant load on the medial delt through the entire arc, including the bottom where dumbbells go slack — pairing this with the dumbbell version earlier maximizes delt stimulus quality.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment allows wrist supination at the bottom, spreading the rope apart to achieve a strong contraction of the lateral head — an effective isolation finisher after the heavier compound tricep work.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline heavy pull — 5 sets on rows, log every weight.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Primary horizontal pull compound — the wide overhand grip emphasizes the upper back, rear delts, and mid-traps, building the thickness and width that defines an advanced back from the rear.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Primary vertical pull for lat width — the wide grip places the lats in a fully lengthened position at the top and allows a strong elbow-down drive that targets the outer lat sweep.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull with constant cable tension through the full range — trains mid-back thickness and scapular retraction strength that barbell rows in a fixed hinge position cannot fully isolate.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the lats by removing bicep contribution entirely — keeping the arm straight forces the lat to perform the full pulldown, producing a strong peak contraction that compound rows don't replicate.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline position stretches the long head of the bicep at the shoulder, training the muscle through a fuller range than standard curls and developing both peak and lower bicep thickness.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip loads the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the bicep long head — the brachialis sits beneath the bicep and when developed pushes it upward, adding visible arm size and thickness.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the high horizontal pressing volume from push days and keeps the shoulder joint healthy under sustained training loads across a 12-week program.

sessions.title: Legs Quad
sessions.sessionFocus: Heavy quad focus — 5 sets back squat, calibrate depth and load.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral lower-body compound — trains quads, glutes, and posterior chain through a loaded knee-dominant pattern that forms the backbone of your quad priority programming this cycle.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Machine-based quad isolation compound — the fixed pad angle keeps the torso upright and places maximum mechanical stress on the quads through a deep range of motion without spinal loading after heavy squats.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg loading exposes bilateral strength imbalances and demands independent quad and glute recruitment per side — more direct quad stretch and mechanical tension than bilateral squats alone.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute isolation compound — trains the glutes at the fully shortened position under heavy load, a stimulus pattern that squats and hinges at longer lengths do not provide.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation finisher — trains the rectus femoris and vastus muscles through knee extension, a movement pattern unavailable in any squat or hinge variation and essential for maximum quad development.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise — trains the ability to resist lumbar hyperextension under load, building the anterior core stability that supports heavy squat and hinge mechanics.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core movement that trains the hip flexors and lower abs through a full range — complements the anti-extension work of the rollout and builds core strength relevant to heavy lower body training.

sessions.title: Push Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume push — higher reps, 5 sets incline, feel the pump.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound anchor for the volume push day — incline barbell pressing accumulates significant mechanical tension on the clavicular head at a rep range optimized for hypertrophy volume.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbell pressing allows greater range of motion than the barbell due to independent arm travel — this stretches the pec fibers at the bottom and increases total muscle damage for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine pressing loads the anterior and medial delt with a guided path, allowing focus on muscular output rather than stabilization — effective for accumulating delt volume safely after heavy push work earlier in the week.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Low to High)
exercises.coachingNote: Low-to-high cable angle targets the upper chest fibers through an arc that matches the direction of the clavicular pec fibers — a different vector from the high-to-low used on Monday for full chest coverage.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Second medial delt session this week through a different loading tool — dumbbell lateral raises at a higher rep range on the volume day accumulate additional shoulder width stimulus beyond what heavy pressing provides.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead cable position stretches the long head of the tricep under load — the long head crosses the shoulder joint and is maximally recruited only when the arm is raised, making overhead extension unique for complete tricep development.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment provides a semi-neutral grip that emphasizes the lateral head of the tricep — pairing this with the rope overhead extension from earlier covers both the long and lateral heads in one volume session.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly isolates the sternal pec fibers through horizontal adduction without tricep involvement — allows maximal chest contraction as a finisher after fatigue has accumulated in the pressing muscles.

sessions.title: Pull Volume
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume pull — 5 sets lat pulldown, log loads for next week.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts lat pulldown emphasis toward the lower lats and involves the biceps more actively in the pull — a different stimulus angle from Monday's wide grip pulldown for complete lat development.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip cable row targets the upper back and rear delts with a horizontal pull that differs from the close-grip patterns — the wider hand spacing increases upper trap and rear delt engagement during the row.

exercises.name: Chest Supported Row
exercises.coachingNote: Chest-supported position eliminates momentum and lower back assistance — every rep is pure mid-back and lat work, making this effective for accumulating high-quality volume without the spinal fatigue of heavy barbell rows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral row that allows a longer range of motion than bilateral variations — each side works independently, removing compensatory patterns and building mid-back thickness and lat density per side.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The EZ bar curl loads both bicep heads and the brachialis through a semi-supinated grip that reduces wrist strain — effective for accumulating overall bicep mass volume on the second pull day of the week.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Preacher pad pins the upper arm in place and removes any swinging, isolating the short head of the bicep through a fully constrained range — this is where bicep peak and lower bicep fullness are developed.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation through a horizontal abduction pattern — the cable maintains tension through the full arc unlike dumbbells, providing a second rear delt session this week to balance the pushing volume accumulated across both push days.

sessions.title: Legs Posterior
sessions.sessionFocus: Posterior volume — hamstrings and glutes leading, 5 sets RDL.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hamstring hinge for this session — the stiff-leg variation maintains a more upright shin angle than Romanian deadlift, increasing spinal flexion and placing greater stretch demand on the hamstrings through their entire length.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust loads the glutes at full hip extension — this is the strongest position for glute recruitment and the machine version allows heavier loading with better stability than the barbell version on a fatigued posterior chain.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semitendinosus through their knee-flexor function, a role the hip hinge movements above cannot fully address, making this essential for complete hamstring development.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius and minimus through hip abduction — these outer glute fibers are undertrained by thrust and hinge patterns alone and contribute directly to hip shape, lateral stability, and knee tracking under load.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip flexed during the curl, placing the hamstrings on greater stretch at the start of each rep compared to lying leg curl — a different stimulus vector to maximize hamstring priority volume this week.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Priority quad exercise added to this posterior session — your quad development goal requires volume on every lower body day, and leg press after hinges and curls allows quad loading without taxing the spinal structures already worked.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through full plantar flexion with the knee extended — the gastrocnemius crosses both the knee and ankle, so it must be loaded with a straight leg to recruit it fully alongside the soleus.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee-flexed position takes the gastrocnemius off tension and isolates the soleus — the soleus is the deeper, denser calf muscle and requires knee-bent loading that the standing variation cannot adequately provide.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral lower-body compound — trains quads, glutes, and posterior chain through a loaded knee-dominant pattern that forms the backbone of your quad priority programming this cycle.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Machine-based quad isolation compound — the fixed pad angle keeps the torso upright and places maximum mechanical stress on the quads through a deep range of motion without spinal loading after heavy squats.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg loading exposes bilateral strength imbalances and demands independent quad and glute recruitment per side — more direct quad stretch and mechanical tension than bilateral squats alone.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Primary glute isolation compound — trains the glutes at the fully shortened position under heavy load, a stimulus pattern that squats and hinges at longer lengths do not provide.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Direct quad isolation finisher — trains the rectus femoris and vastus muscles through knee extension, a movement pattern unavailable in any squat or hinge variation and essential for maximum quad development.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise — trains the ability to resist lumbar hyperextension under load, building the anterior core stability that supports heavy squat and hinge mechanics.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core movement that trains the hip flexors and lower abs through a full range — complements the anti-extension work of the rollout and builds core strength relevant to heavy lower body training.

days.title: Push Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume push — higher reps, 5 sets incline, feel the pump.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound anchor for the volume push day — incline barbell pressing accumulates significant mechanical tension on the clavicular head at a rep range optimized for hypertrophy volume.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Dumbbell pressing allows greater range of motion than the barbell due to independent arm travel — this stretches the pec fibers at the bottom and increases total muscle damage for hypertrophy.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine pressing loads the anterior and medial delt with a guided path, allowing focus on muscular output rather than stabilization — effective for accumulating delt volume safely after heavy push work earlier in the week.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Low to High)
exercises.coachingNote: Low-to-high cable angle targets the upper chest fibers through an arc that matches the direction of the clavicular pec fibers — a different vector from the high-to-low used on Monday for full chest coverage.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Second medial delt session this week through a different loading tool — dumbbell lateral raises at a higher rep range on the volume day accumulate additional shoulder width stimulus beyond what heavy pressing provides.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension (Rope)
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead cable position stretches the long head of the tricep under load — the long head crosses the shoulder joint and is maximally recruited only when the arm is raised, making overhead extension unique for complete tricep development.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment provides a semi-neutral grip that emphasizes the lateral head of the tricep — pairing this with the rope overhead extension from earlier covers both the long and lateral heads in one volume session.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly isolates the sternal pec fibers through horizontal adduction without tricep involvement — allows maximal chest contraction as a finisher after fatigue has accumulated in the pressing muscles.

days.title: Pull Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume pull — 5 sets lat pulldown, log loads for next week.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts lat pulldown emphasis toward the lower lats and involves the biceps more actively in the pull — a different stimulus angle from Monday's wide grip pulldown for complete lat development.

exercises.name: Cable Row (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide grip cable row targets the upper back and rear delts with a horizontal pull that differs from the close-grip patterns — the wider hand spacing increases upper trap and rear delt engagement during the row.

exercises.name: Chest Supported Row
exercises.coachingNote: Chest-supported position eliminates momentum and lower back assistance — every rep is pure mid-back and lat work, making this effective for accumulating high-quality volume without the spinal fatigue of heavy barbell rows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral row that allows a longer range of motion than bilateral variations — each side works independently, removing compensatory patterns and building mid-back thickness and lat density per side.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The EZ bar curl loads both bicep heads and the brachialis through a semi-supinated grip that reduces wrist strain — effective for accumulating overall bicep mass volume on the second pull day of the week.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Preacher pad pins the upper arm in place and removes any swinging, isolating the short head of the bicep through a fully constrained range — this is where bicep peak and lower bicep fullness are developed.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation through a horizontal abduction pattern — the cable maintains tension through the full arc unlike dumbbells, providing a second rear delt session this week to balance the pushing volume accumulated across both push days.

days.title: Legs Posterior
days.sessionFocus: Posterior volume — hamstrings and glutes leading, 5 sets RDL.

exercises.name: Stiff Leg Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Primary hamstring hinge for this session — the stiff-leg variation maintains a more upright shin angle than Romanian deadlift, increasing spinal flexion and placing greater stretch demand on the hamstrings through their entire length.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Machine hip thrust loads the glutes at full hip extension — this is the strongest position for glute recruitment and the machine version allows heavier loading with better stability than the barbell version on a fatigued posterior chain.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — trains the biceps femoris and semitendinosus through their knee-flexor function, a role the hip hinge movements above cannot fully address, making this essential for complete hamstring development.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius and minimus through hip abduction — these outer glute fibers are undertrained by thrust and hinge patterns alone and contribute directly to hip shape, lateral stability, and knee tracking under load.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip flexed during the curl, placing the hamstrings on greater stretch at the start of each rep compared to lying leg curl — a different stimulus vector to maximize hamstring priority volume this week.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Priority quad exercise added to this posterior session — your quad development goal requires volume on every lower body day, and leg press after hinges and curls allows quad loading without taxing the spinal structures already worked.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through full plantar flexion with the knee extended — the gastrocnemius crosses both the knee and ankle, so it must be loaded with a straight leg to recruit it fully alongside the soleus.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee-flexed position takes the gastrocnemius off tension and isolates the soleus — the soleus is the deeper, denser calf muscle and requires knee-bent loading that the standing variation cannot adequately provide.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push — trains the pecs, anterior delts, and triceps together as your foundational chest movement for this plan.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width — the wide grip targets the outer portion of the lats and teaches you to drive your elbows down, the key movement pattern for back development.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary bilateral lower body compound — builds quads, glutes, and overall leg mass as the cornerstone movement of every Full Body A session.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core work — builds the midline stability needed to maintain a rigid torso during squats and bench, protecting your spine under load.

sessions.title: Full Body B
sessions.sessionFocus: Calibration lower and shoulder day — 3 sets, RPE 7 target.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.coachingNote: Primary overhead pressing movement — develops front and lateral delt strength and mass, with dumbbells allowing natural shoulder rotation that suits beginners well.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness through the rhomboids and mid traps — pairs with the vertical pull from Monday to ensure complete back development across the week.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge movement that loads the hamstrings and glutes through a long range of motion — balances the quad-dominant work from Full Body A and builds posterior chain strength.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core drill that trains opposite arm and leg coordination while keeping the lumbar spine flat — builds the deep core stability that transfers directly to every compound lift.

sessions.title: Full Body A
sessions.sessionFocus: Repeat Full Body A — match your Monday logs and hit 3 sets.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Incline angle shifts the pressing stimulus toward the upper chest — varying from Monday's flat bench ensures the clavicular head of the pec receives direct development across the week.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Underhand)
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull with an underhand grip that emphasises the lats and lower mid-back — the grip change from Monday's pulldown completes the back stimulus with a different pulling angle.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Machine-based quad compound that allows high loading with reduced spinal demand — varies the stimulus from Monday's back squat and accumulates additional quad volume to close out the week.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core movement that trains the rectus abdominis and hip flexors through their full range — provides a different stimulus from the anti-extension work earlier in the week.

sessions.title: Upper Body

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push compound — trains the pecs, anterior delt, and triceps together and sets the baseline load data for chest progression across this plan.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Upper back and lat thickness through a horizontal pull — wide overhand grip targets the mid-traps and rhomboids to balance the pressing volume in this session.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Vertical pull that develops lat width — pairing a vertical pull with the horizontal row ensures both planes of back development are addressed in this session.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing does not adequately develop this head, so direct lateral work is included here to build the full shoulder shape.

sessions.title: Lower Body

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Primary bilateral knee-dominant compound — builds quad, glute, and core strength together and establishes your squat baseline for progressive loading across the 12 weeks.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Direct glute isolation through hip extension — places maximum tension on the glutes at peak contraction, a stimulus the squat and RDL do not fully replicate.

exercises.name: Leg Extension

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core stability — trains the deep trunk musculature that supports spinal position under load during squats and hinges.

sessions.title: Upper Hypertrophy
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume upper — back and arms, 3 sets per exercise at RPE 7.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pull that builds mid-back thickness and lat engagement through a constant-tension cable stimulus — a different feel to the barbell row from Monday, targeting overlapping but distinct portions of the back.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip shifts lat pulldown emphasis toward the lower lats and biceps — paired with the cable row to cover both vertical and horizontal back planes in this session.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt and external rotator work — balances the horizontal pressing volume from Monday and keeps shoulder health in check across the training week.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl (Wide Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Bilateral bicep compound — the short head and brachialis are the primary targets here, building overall arm thickness and complementing the pulling volume in this session.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Rope attachment allows the hands to separate at the bottom, maximising lateral head contraction — direct tricep isolation to develop arm size alongside the bicep work in this session.

sessions.title: Lower Hypertrophy
sessions.sessionFocus: Volume lower — glutes and hamstrings priority, log every set at RPE 7.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg compound that challenges quad and glute strength unilaterally — exposes and corrects left-right imbalances that bilateral squatting can mask over time.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Hamstring isolation through knee flexion — directly targets the biceps femoris and semitendinosus where hinges leave off, adding dedicated curl volume on this posterior-focused day.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge driven by glute and hamstring tension against cable resistance — keeps constant load through the movement and serves as a glute-dominant accessory without the spinal loading of a barbell hinge.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Quad isolation finisher that provides direct rectus femoris stimulus to complement the single-leg compound work earlier in the session.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that challenges the entire anterior core under a long lever — a more demanding progression from the plank used earlier in the week.

sessions.title: Push Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Baseline push — 5 sets on bench, calibrate your loads.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push compound — trains the pectorals, anterior delt, and triceps through a full pressing range and anchors chest volume for the week.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts emphasis to the clavicular head of the pec — a balanced chest development requires dedicated upper chest work alongside flat pressing.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Mid Cable)
exercises.coachingNote: Cable flyes maintain constant tension through the full range of motion, providing a pec stretch and squeeze that barbell pressing cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing alone does not adequately develop this head and dedicated lateral work is necessary.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the anterior deltoid through a controlled arc — the cable angle maintains tension at the top of the movement where dumbbells go slack.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Trains all three heads of the tricep through the full press range with a load capacity far above isolation movements — your primary tricep mass builder.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: The rope attachment allows wrist supination at the bottom, spreading the handles to fully contract the lateral head — excellent shape and definition stimulus for the tricep.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a stretched state, which is the most growth-prone position for that head — essential for tricep mass.

sessions.title: Pull Heavy
sessions.sessionFocus: Priority pull day — 5 sets of weighted pull-ups, lat focus.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary vertical pull — weighted pull-ups are the single best exercise for lat width and thickness, and the top priority movement for your back development goal.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide overhand grip targets the upper back and rear delt more than a close grip — pairs with the vertical pull to cover both planes of lat and mid-back development.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Close Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Close grip shifts the elbow path behind the torso at the bottom, increasing the lat stretch and peak contraction relative to a wide-grip variation — added lat volume for your priority muscle.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pulling builds mid-back thickness through the rhomboids and lower traps — constant cable tension through the full range makes this a reliable volume accumulator.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Keeps the biceps out of the movement by maintaining a straight arm, forcing the lats to work in isolation — excellent lat activation exercise that supports your lat-width priority.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline position places the humerus behind the torso, stretching the long head of the bicep at the start of each rep — the most effective single exercise for long-head development.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip hammer curls heavily recruit the brachialis and the long head of the bicep — builds arm thickness and peak alongside the incline curl variation above.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Cable behind the body keeps the long head of the bicep loaded in its stretched position throughout the curl — extra priority volume targeting your specified long-head bias.

sessions.title: Legs Full (Quad Focus)

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary bilateral lower body compound — develops quad, glute, and posterior chain strength through the full movement pattern that forms the foundation of your lower training.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The machine-supported position allows the torso to stay upright, increasing knee travel and placing greater tension on the quad through a deeper range than the barbell squat.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg loading identifies and corrects bilateral asymmetries while demanding greater quad and glute activation per leg than most bilateral movements.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the hamstrings through knee flexion, a function the Romanian deadlift cannot fully train — necessary for complete hamstring development across both hip and knee actions.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the rectus femoris and VMO through knee extension — the only exercise in this session that fully trains the quad without glute or hamstring assistance.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower abdominals and hip flexors through a full range — complements the anti-extension stimulus of the rollout.

exercises.name: Pec Deck

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row

exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation balances the heavy horizontal pressing volume from Monday — keeps the shoulder joint healthy and trains the posterior capsule that pressing neglects.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: A second bicep session this week supports your priority volume target — EZ bar curl trains the short head and overall bicep mass with a joint-friendly wrist angle.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: The elbow-fixed position keeps the long head of the tricep under tension through a large range of motion — one of the best mass builders for the back of the arm.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment locks the wrists in a neutral position and focuses stress on the lateral and medial heads — a different stimulus from the rope used on Monday.

sessions.title: Lower Volume

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes in a lengthened position — your primary compound for this posterior chain session, accumulating volume at moderate intensity.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius through hip abduction — the medius is undertrained by most posterior chain work and contributes to both glute development and hip stability.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral hinge that demands balance and isolates each hamstring independently — identifies asymmetries and accumulates additional hamstring volume at lower absolute load.

days.sessionFocus: Baseline push — 5 sets on bench, calibrate your loads.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary horizontal push compound — trains the pectorals, anterior delt, and triceps through a full pressing range and anchors chest volume for the week.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: The incline angle shifts emphasis to the clavicular head of the pec — a balanced chest development requires dedicated upper chest work alongside flat pressing.

exercises.name: Cable Fly (Mid Cable)
exercises.coachingNote: Cable flyes maintain constant tension through the full range of motion, providing a pec stretch and squeeze that barbell pressing cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the medial deltoid for shoulder width — compound pressing alone does not adequately develop this head and dedicated lateral work is necessary.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the anterior deltoid through a controlled arc — the cable angle maintains tension at the top of the movement where dumbbells go slack.

exercises.name: Close Grip Bench Press
exercises.coachingNote: Trains all three heads of the tricep through the full press range with a load capacity far above isolation movements — your primary tricep mass builder.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: The rope attachment allows wrist supination at the bottom, spreading the handles to fully contract the lateral head — excellent shape and definition stimulus for the tricep.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Overhead position places the long head of the tricep in a stretched state, which is the most growth-prone position for that head — essential for tricep mass.

days.title: Pull Heavy
days.sessionFocus: Priority pull day — 5 sets of weighted pull-ups, lat focus.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary vertical pull — weighted pull-ups are the single best exercise for lat width and thickness, and the top priority movement for your back development goal.

exercises.name: Barbell Row (Overhand Wide)
exercises.coachingNote: Wide overhand grip targets the upper back and rear delt more than a close grip — pairs with the vertical pull to cover both planes of lat and mid-back development.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Close Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Close grip shifts the elbow path behind the torso at the bottom, increasing the lat stretch and peak contraction relative to a wide-grip variation — added lat volume for your priority muscle.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.coachingNote: Horizontal pulling builds mid-back thickness through the rhomboids and lower traps — constant cable tension through the full range makes this a reliable volume accumulator.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Pulldown
exercises.coachingNote: Keeps the biceps out of the movement by maintaining a straight arm, forcing the lats to work in isolation — excellent lat activation exercise that supports your lat-width priority.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.coachingNote: The incline position places the humerus behind the torso, stretching the long head of the bicep at the start of each rep — the most effective single exercise for long-head development.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Neutral grip hammer curls heavily recruit the brachialis and the long head of the bicep — builds arm thickness and peak alongside the incline curl variation above.

exercises.name: Bayesian Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Cable behind the body keeps the long head of the bicep loaded in its stretched position throughout the curl — extra priority volume targeting your specified long-head bias.

days.title: Legs Full (Quad Focus)
days.sessionFocus: Heavy quad focus — 5 sets back squat, log your depth.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Your primary bilateral lower body compound — develops quad, glute, and posterior chain strength through the full movement pattern that forms the foundation of your lower training.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.coachingNote: The machine-supported position allows the torso to stay upright, increasing knee travel and placing greater tension on the quad through a deeper range than the barbell squat.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.coachingNote: Quad volume without spinal loading — lets you push leg intensity after your primary compound.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.coachingNote: Single-leg loading identifies and corrects bilateral asymmetries while demanding greater quad and glute activation per leg than most bilateral movements.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the hamstrings through knee flexion, a function the Romanian deadlift cannot fully train — necessary for complete hamstring development across both hip and knee actions.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.coachingNote: Isolates the rectus femoris and VMO through knee extension — the only exercise in this session that fully trains the quad without glute or hamstring assistance.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-extension core exercise that trains the rectus abdominis and deep stabilisers under a significant lengthened load — one of the highest-demand core movements available.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Flexion-based core exercise that trains the lower abdominals and hip flexors through a full range — complements the anti-extension stimulus of the rollout.

days.title: Upper Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume upper — chest, back, arms at 5 sets each.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.coachingNote: Upper chest compound on a volume day — the barbell version allows heavier loading than dumbbell incline, accumulating quality volume for the clavicular head of the pec.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.coachingNote: Machine fly that isolates the pec through horizontal adduction with full control over the range — ideal for volume accumulation without loading the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (Reverse Grip)
exercises.coachingNote: Reverse grip rotates the elbows in toward the body, improving lat engagement at the bottom of the movement and recruiting the biceps as a strong secondary mover.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral horizontal pull that allows a greater range of motion and lat stretch than the barbell row — accumulates mid-back thickness volume for your priority muscle.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
exercises.coachingNote: Rear delt isolation balances the heavy horizontal pressing volume from Monday — keeps the shoulder joint healthy and trains the posterior capsule that pressing neglects.

exercises.name: EZ Bar Curl
exercises.coachingNote: A second bicep session this week supports your priority volume target — EZ bar curl trains the short head and overall bicep mass with a joint-friendly wrist angle.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
exercises.coachingNote: The elbow-fixed position keeps the long head of the tricep under tension through a large range of motion — one of the best mass builders for the back of the arm.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown (V-Bar)
exercises.coachingNote: V-bar attachment locks the wrists in a neutral position and focuses stress on the lateral and medial heads — a different stimulus from the rope used on Monday.

days.title: Lower Volume
days.sessionFocus: Volume lower — hamstrings and glutes, 5 sets each movement.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.coachingNote: Hip hinge that loads the hamstrings and glutes in a lengthened position — your primary compound for this posterior chain session, accumulating volume at moderate intensity.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the glutes at end-range hip extension where they are strongest — the horizontal loading vector produces a peak contraction that the Romanian deadlift cannot replicate.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.coachingNote: Seated position keeps the hip flexed, which stretches the hamstring and increases the range of motion compared to lying leg curl — maximises the muscle length stimulus.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.coachingNote: Targets the gluteus medius through hip abduction — the medius is undertrained by most posterior chain work and contributes to both glute development and hip stability.

exercises.name: Single Leg RDL
exercises.coachingNote: Unilateral hinge that demands balance and isolates each hamstring independently — identifies asymmetries and accumulates additional hamstring volume at lower absolute load.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Trains the gastrocnemius through full plantar flexion with the knee extended — the straight-leg position is required to maximally recruit the gastrocnemius as opposed to the soleus.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.coachingNote: Knee-bent position reduces gastrocnemius contribution and isolates the soleus — the soleus makes up a significant portion of calf mass and requires its own dedicated work.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.coachingNote: Anti-rotation core exercise that trains the obliques and deep stabilisers under rotational load — a different stimulus from the flexion and anti-extension work done on Wednesday.
